rows.note: Use 嬲 as the all-purpose choice when someone is angry, distressed, or unhappy.

example.english: I'm really upset and don't want to talk to him.
example.traditional: 我真係嬲，唔想同佢講嘢。
example.jyutping: ngo5 zan1 hai6 nau1 m4 soeng2 tung4 keoi5 gong2 je5

rows.note: Use this as the all-purpose way to say that something causes a person emotional distress or unhappiness.

example.english: The way you said that upset me.
example.jyutping: nei5 gam3 joeng2 gong2 ling6 ngo5 m4 hoi1 sam1

rows.note: Use this specifically when the person is made angry rather than merely unhappy or distressed.

example.english: You really upset me by scolding me in front of so many people.
example.traditional: 你當住咁多人鬧我，真係激嬲我喎。
example.jyutping: nei5 dong1 zyu6 gam3 do1 jan4 naau6 ngo5 zan1 hai6 gik1 nau1 ngo5 wo3

rows.note: Use 唔舒服 when upset means feeling physically unwell, nauseated, or ready to vomit.

example.english: My stomach feels upset, and I feel like vomiting.
example.jyutping: ngo5 go3 wai6 hou2 m4 syu1 fuk6 soeng2 au2

rows.note: Use this when something throws an arrangement, plan, system, or balance into disorder.

example.english: This heavy rain upset our plans.
example.traditional: 呢場大雨打亂咗我哋嘅計劃。
example.jyutping: ni1 coeng4 daai6 jyu5 daa2 lyun6 zo2 ngo5 dei6 ge3 gai3 waak6

rows.note: Use this when upsetting something means damaging or adversely affecting an existing balance or system.

example.english: This change upset the balance of the whole system.
example.traditional: 呢個改動破壞咗成個系統嘅平衡。
example.jyutping: ni1 go3 goi2 dung6 po3 waai6 zo2 seng4 go3 hai6 tung2 ge3 ping4 hang4
